result.summary: A residential street with continuous sidewalks and mature street trees providing shade and a partial buffer. The environment lacks formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure, traffic calming, or lane markings, which may lead to unpredictable vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible at the intersection or midblock, requiring pedestrians to cross without designated protection.

hazards.name: Unmarked wide roadway
hazards.description: The absence of lane markings on a wide residential street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and poor lane discipline.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures like speed humps to maintain low vehicle speeds in this residential area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a discontinuous sidewalk that transitions into an unpaved dirt surface, creating significant accessibility challenges. A wide paved driveway and a lack of road markings or traffic calming measures prioritize vehicle movement over pedestrian safety in this residential setting.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The paved walkway ends abruptly, forcing pedestrians onto unpaved and potentially uneven dirt and grass terrain.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the foreground walkway

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: A large paved driveway area increases the exposure of pedestrians to turning vehicles and lacks clear demarcation.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left paved area crossing the sidewalk path

interventions.title: Sidewalk Extension
interventions.description: Complete the paved sidewalk network by extending the walkway through the unpaved section to provide a continuous, accessible path.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the driveway entrance to minimize pedestrian exposure and slow down entering vehicles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by fragmented and narrow sidewalks with no marked crossings or traffic calming measures. The lack of lane markings and the presence of parked vehicles on unpaved shoulders further degrade the safety and accessibility for people walking.

hazards.name: Fragmented and Poor Sidewalks
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is discontinuous and unpaved in sections, while the sidewalk on the right is extremely narrow and lacks a buffer from traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or signage indicating where pedestrians should cross the street.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Vehicles parked on the unpaved shoulder on the left may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction and Completion
interventions.description: Install continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street with a minimum width of 5 feet.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps at intersections to provide safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming and Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add lane markings to define travel lanes and implement traffic calming measures like speed humps to reduce vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow sidewalk that is significantly obstructed by a large tree and a utility pole, forcing pedestrians into a very tight space. There is no buffer between the walkway and the adjacent on-street parking, which reduces the overall sense of safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A large tree trunk and a utility pole occupy most of the sidewalk width, creating a pinch point that is likely impassable for wheelchairs or strollers.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to parked vehicles and the travel lane with no horizontal separation or furniture zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line where the white SUV is parked

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk into the parking lane to provide a clear walking path around the existing tree and utility pole.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions or 'bulb-outs' to create more space for pedestrians and reduce the effective crossing distance if an intersection is nearby.
